- `create-or-reuse` — create the task branch, or reuse the recorded one.
- `reuse-required` — reuse the recorded `branch:`; refuse without one.

  `manual`.

authoritative: workflow name, step name, skills, a local edit of the step's
skill or section, `assignee:` and `requires:` do not change it. Customize the
procedure and its instructions freely; the checkout follows the declaration.

| `code/with-self-review` | `self-qa` | `reuse-required` |
| `code/agent-merge`, `code/design-then-implement`, `code/with-review`, `docs/with-review` | `open-pr` | `control` |
| `code/with-self-review` | `pr` | `control` |
| `code/agent-merge` | `merge` | `reuse-required` |

Every other packaged workflow omits the field and freezes `manual`.

No command rewrites a frozen ticket to add `checkout:`. The fallback may be

   remote; ahead or diverged commits are kept and reported), or one created
   from its remote tip. It refuses — on control, starting nothing — a
   recorded branch absent everywhere, a reuse step with no branch (unless
   `## Already satisfied` evidence exists: the agent then verifies from
   control), a branch committing ticket intent control lacks ([stranded
   ticket writes](#stranded-ticket-writes)), one held by another worktree,
   or ignored files the switch would overwrite. After switching it projects
   only this ticket from control, unstaged: the session's only entry dirt.

   `commit -a`. Never stage, commit, or restore the projected ticket. A

   with it. Left dirty, it is
   [held for merge](../state-publication/SKILL.md#held-for-merge-on-feature-checkouts):
   the sweep does not publish it, and return refuses until it is committed

# Manual start, work, end

Part of [coga/checkouts](../SKILL.md), which owns the launched lifecycle and
which checkout each step starts in.

## Procedure

Use this when no `COGA_LAUNCH_RETURNS_CHECKOUT=1` witness is set — manual or
API sessions, megalaunch picks, exempt checkouts — and before editing in a
step whose runtime notice says launch set up no branch (manual policy, or a
control step that must exceptionally change code). The agent performs both
moves:

1. **Start check.** `git fetch origin main`, then require HEAD on `main`, a
   clean tree with Coga state included, and a successful `git merge
   --ff-only origin/main`. Launch regenerates the ignored
   `coga/.agent-skills/` view; a repo initialized before `coga init` wrote
   that ignore rule sees it as dirt — add `.agent-skills/` to
   `coga/.gitignore`, never commit it. Anything else — dirty files, another
   ticket's branch, a diverged `main` — means stop: ask the attending human,
   or `coga block` in a queue run. Do not work around an occupied checkout
   with a linked worktree, a control checkout, a stash, or a switch.
2. **Work.** Write ticket state (`branch:` under `## Dev` once created with
   `git branch <name>`, plan notes) on `main`, publish it (below), then
   switch to the feature branch and change code only; ticket edits made
   there are not published until the next sweep. A resumed branch is reused:
   switch to it and `git rebase` onto fetched `origin/main`.
3. **End.** Commit, push the branch (`git push -u origin <branch>`, or
   `--force-with-lease` after a rebase), then return:
   - `git fetch origin main`;
   - for every dirty path under the Coga roots, verify it is already on
     `origin/main` by the rules of
     [the launch boundary](../launch-boundary/SKILL.md) (`git diff --quiet origin/main -- <path>`;
     for `coga/log.md`, every added line is on `origin/main`) and discard it
     (`git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree -- <path>`). `git diff`
     skips untracked files, so compare an untracked one with
     `git show origin/main:<path> | cmp - <path>` and delete it only when
     identical;
   - `git switch main`, then `git merge --ff-only origin/main`.

   If any dirty path under the Coga roots is *not* already on `origin/main`,
   or any other path is dirty, stop and escalate. A knowledge file the sweep
   [held for merge](../../state-publication/SKILL.md#held-for-merge-on-feature-checkouts)
   belongs in the branch's commit (or redone on `main`), not discarded. Never discard unpublished
   state. Then write the step's handoff on `main` and run `coga bump`, which
   publishes it. The session leaves the checkout on `main`, clean.

## Publish pre-branch ticket edits

Writing `branch:` or plan notes on `main` does not publish them: Git carries
uncommitted edits across a branch switch. Before switching, publish those
edits strictly, naming each edited file. The recipe resolves paths against
the current directory, which launch preserves, so anchor them at the checkout
root:

```sh
coga run publish-state "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/coga/tasks/<slug>.md"
git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all
```

Exit 0 means every named file is confirmed on control; any non-zero exit
(contract in [strict publication on
demand](../../state-publication/SKILL.md#strict-publication-on-demand))
is the stop signal. Use the status check only for dirty files you did not name,
and require it to be empty before switching. Do not fall back to calling the
sweep through a `python -c` one-liner: the sweep reports publication failures
without raising, and the shell's `python` often cannot import Coga at all. If
publication fails or the tree remains dirty, stop and escalate; do not switch,
stash, or commit the ticket edit on the feature branch. The same publication applies to a
sandbox clone's `worktree:` record in the primary checkout, before starting
work in the clone.

name: coga/checkouts/reconciliation
description: Main as the shared source of truth for all agent edits, freshness checkpoints, preserving unique work during reconciliation, and when conflicts need human judgment.
---

# Reconcile work with moving main

The configured remote control branch (`origin/main` by default) is the source of
truth for shared repository state. A local checkout and the launch prompt are
snapshots; expect main to advance during a session. This applies to all agent
edits, including code, documentation, contexts, skills, workflows, tickets,
and bootstrap or ad-hoc work. A fresh launch does not guarantee a fresh handoff.

## Freshness checkpoints

Before editing, fetch current main and inspect changes relevant to the work,
including its governing instructions. Before publishing or handing off edits,
fetch again and reconcile against that tip. Read-only work needs no merge;
qualify conclusions tied to an older revision if relevant files changed.
Git-disabled or remote-less work cannot claim remote freshness; report that
limitation when handing off changes.

## Preserve both sides

Reconciliation preserves main's newer work and the still-needed local intent:

- For committed branch work, merge or rebase current main using the owning
  workflow's procedure ([code branch procedure](../SKILL.md#start-work-end)).
  Resolve straightforward conflicts yourself; a clean Git merge still needs
  inspection for changes in meaning or assumptions.
- For uncommitted edits, inspect the branch's committed changes as well as
  its staged and unstaged deltas and main's intervening changes. Preserve the
  dirty deltas in patches or file copies, including untracked files, and
  record the original branch HEAD. Verify those backups before clearing any
  dirty files. Restore tracked files and the index from the branch's own
  HEAD, merge or rebase current main, then reapply the still-needed dirty
  deltas onto the resulting branch, resolving conflicts there. Do not replace
  a feature file with main's version first: that also removes committed
  branch work which a working-tree patch does not contain.
- For a stale ticket publication or a handoff, preserve unpublished prose
  and blackboard notes before refreshing the ticket from control. Account
  for committed local intent as well as dirty edits; reconcile the intended
  changes onto control's current ticket while respecting CLI-owned lifecycle
  fields. This ticket-specific recovery is not a recipe for replacing code
  files with main's version. Never replay a transition merely because its
  publication failed; use the publication recovery described in the
  [handoff procedure](../SKILL.md#in-a-launched-session).

If any work already landed, prove that from history and content before dropping
the duplicate. Preserve the owning definition and reconcile dependent references.

## Sync a feature branch with control

Every Coga command run from a feature or detached checkout publishes the
ticket and log it changed to control and leaves those files dirty in that
checkout by design ([state publication](../../state-publication/SKILL.md#control-versus-feature-checkouts)).
A new ticket stays untracked. That dirt blocks `git merge` or `git rebase` of
control until it is dropped.

Drop it only when every dirty or untracked file under the Coga and contexts
roots already equals control. Each such file must be a regular file whose
bytes (after clean filters) and mode equal the copy in the local
`<remote>/<control>` ref. A tracked file must also have no staged change.
`coga status` checks this against local refs (fetch first for a current
answer). When it holds, `coga status` prints the exact command, anchored to
the Git root, with paths quoted for the current shell. On POSIX it has this
shape, and any part with no paths is left out:

```bash
git --literal-pathspecs -C <root> checkout -- <tracked…> && rm -- <untracked…> && git -C <root> merge --no-edit <remote>/<control>
```

Native Windows PowerShell gets the same steps with `Remove-Item -LiteralPath`,
each nested in `if ($?) { … }`. `git merge --autostash` is not enough: it sets
aside tracked dirt, but an untracked ticket identical to control still aborts
the merge ("untracked working tree files would be overwritten"). Prefer merge
over rebase for a branch that is already pushed, so it needs no force-push.

When `coga status` instead lists files that differ, are staged, have another
mode, or are deleted, do not use the command. Publish differing routine state
(tickets, the log) first (`coga run publish-state`), then check again. A file
[held for merge](../../state-publication/SKILL.md#held-for-merge-on-feature-checkouts)
cannot be published from the branch: commit it on the branch for review, or
redo it on control. Otherwise reconcile those files by hand as in
[Preserve both sides](#preserve-both-sides).

## Verify and escalate

Inspect the combined diff and run checks appropriate to the affected work
after reconciliation. If publication reports that main moved again, repeat
the comparison against the new tip. Normal movement is not itself a blocker.
Escalate per session conduct when intent conflicts, ownership is unclear, or
access prevents reconciliation; identify the conflicting changes and the
decision or capability needed. Never choose main's entire file blindly,
discard unique work to silence sync, or bypass a publication or lifecycle
guard. These rules do not authorize taking over another task's dirty checkout
or crossing a human approval gate.

name: coga/knowledge
description: The permanent authoring rule for Coga knowledge — which surface owns a fact, one owner per fact, links never load content, when to attach versus cite a topic, and the topic size review policy.
---

# Where knowledge lives

Every fact has exactly one owning file; when two copies disagree, the owner
is right. Choose the owner by what the knowledge is:

| Knowledge | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| Shared facts and contracts: behavior, invariants, edge cases, product intent used across capabilities | a local topic under the configured contexts root (`<ref>/SKILL.md`), or the package owner of a shipped topic |
| Reusable process: how to do a thing | a skill (`coga/skills/<ref>/SKILL.md` or bundled) |
| One ticket-defined capability's behavior and procedure | its command ticket (`bootstrap/<name>/ticket.md`) or recurring template (`recurring/<name>/ticket.md`) |
| Maintenance procedures specific to that capability | supporting files beside its persistent ticket, linked for reading when needed |
| Per-ticket field guide: a summary carried by new tickets that links the owning topics | inline ticket template (`src/coga/resources/ticket.md`) |
| One task's temporary working state | that ticket's blackboard ([coga/blackboard](../blackboard/SKILL.md)) |
| Execution history | `coga/log.md`, written only by CLI commands |
| Dated evidence, completed investigations, archived proposals, and other retired history | the repo's dated archive, outside the contexts root |

Humans and agents read the same owning file. Do not keep a short agent
rendition beside a longer human one: that is two owners of one fact, and the
copies drift independently. For shared facts, pick the topic whose subject
already covers the neighbouring facts; when two fit, the more narrowly
attached one wins, because the fact then costs tokens only where it is needed.

Durability alone does not make a document a context. Command tickets and
recurring templates persist; their individual executions and period tasks do
not. Keep a job's contract with the job: phone-home owns its snapshot boundary,
and Dream owns its phase order. Extract shared facts into a context and
reusable procedures into a skill when other capabilities need them.

Keep maintenance instructions separate from instructions for each run. A
template may link a sibling runbook, but recurring creation copies only
`ticket.py`, not supporting Markdown. Name the persistent template path when
directing a period to a supporting file; do not assume it is beside that
period's ticket. Skills and runbooks remain readable documentation for humans.

An owner decision *not* to act ("we looked at X and chose not to do it") is
product intent, so it belongs with X's standing owner: the shared topic, skill,
command ticket or recurring template, never only the temporary task that
recorded it. The lifecycle retires work tickets and period tasks; a decision
left in one gets re-raised. State what was declined, why, and what would reopen it.

The same retirement breaks links. Retro and `coga delete` remove a ticket
without repairing inbound references, so a topic that names a ticket by path
as the owner of an open question dangles once it retires. Point durable
surfaces at the question's standing owner, not at the transient ticket working
it, and grep for inbound references to a slug before it retires.

## Narrative links, never restates

An index, README, overview, or neighbouring topic may summarize and link to
the owner, but carries no specification-grade detail: no ordered lists, exact
names, counts or field lists that can drift on their own. "Launch stacks
conduct before task material, ticket last; the order is in
`coga/prompt-composition`" is a summary; copying the layer list is a second
specification. Command semantics live with their owning capability. A command
ticket or recurring template owns its own behavior (`bootstrap/retire/ticket.md`
owns `coga retire`); rules several jobs share stay in a topic the ticket links.
`coga/cli` is an index, and installed `coga <cmd> --help` is the syntax authority.

**Sync rule.** A PR that changes an owner greps other surfaces for the fact
and fixes or deletes any restatement in the same PR. No test enforces this
across surfaces; the authoring rule is the enforcement and Dream's knowledge
scan is the backstop. A shipped definition has one committed owner, its
package copy; a repo copy of the same ref is a deliberate local override, a
separate artifact, not a second owner to keep in sync. `CLAUDE.md` /
`AGENTS.md` load in every agent session, so they carry pointers plus only the
rules needed outside `coga launch`, never an owning statement.

## Links do not load content

Composition includes attached refs only
([coga/prompt-composition](../prompt-composition/SKILL.md)). A markdown link
in a topic, skill, or ticket is navigation: the agent reads the target only if
it chooses to open the file, subject to that repo’s access rules. So an
overview does not bring in its children. Knowledge a step requires must be
attached explicitly by ref or named as a required read in the task or skill;
a navigation link alone does neither.

## Attach or cite

Choose from the two audiences defined in
[context layout](../context-layout/SKILL.md#context-audiences): user topics
under `coga/` support operating Coga in adopting repos; the local
Coga-dev set supports developing Coga itself. Select by the task's need,
then apply the attach-or-cite test below. A shipped instruction must resolve
its required knowledge from the user set; a development link is optional
navigation, never a dependency.

For a job-owned contract or supporting file, name its persistent path and the
sections to read in the task's `## Context`. Invoke a reusable skill by ref.
Do not recreate either as a context just to put it in `contexts:`.

`contexts:` is one ticket-wide list, composed whole into every launch of
every step. Decide per ticket across all planned steps:

- **Attach** when a step must have the facts without being told to look:
  its correctness depends on rules spread across the topic, or the author
  cannot predict which facts it will hit. Test: would a launched step go
  wrong if this were absent from the prompt?
- **Cite** when steps need a few identifiable facts from a topic that is
  large relative to the rest of the prompt, or when the ticket will *edit*
  that topic (it gets read first anyway).

Measure relative size at authoring time with `approx_tokens` from
`coga launch --prompt-report`, which skips the state sweep, so a trial
`contexts:` edit stays local; do not edit lifecycle frontmatter to measure,
and do not quote sizes (they go stale). No topic is
always-attach or always-cite.

A cite is one sentence in `## Context` naming the ref and path, saying it is
cited rather than attached, and naming the sections to read, followed by the
facts the step needs, cited as module plus symbol. Do not justify it by size.
The copied facts are a snapshot for that ticket, never a second owner. Citing
does not relax the sync rule: a ticket that changes behavior a cited topic
owns updates that topic and its dependent references in the same PR.

## Topic size review policy

Each topic is a directory holding `SKILL.md` with only `name` and a
one-sentence `description` stating its scope. Targets: 60 to 160 lines and
500 to 1,500 tokens (ceil(chars/4), frontmatter included); overview topics at
most 1,000 tokens. A topic over 200 lines, 10,000 bytes, or 2,500 tokens is
reviewed for a split into narrower leaves in its namespace, so tickets can
attach only the contract they need. An exception needs a recorded reason,
written in the oversized topic itself as one closing `Size exception:`
sentence saying why it stays whole. A reason kept only on a ticket
blackboard or in a PR leaves with them, and the next reader who measures the
topic cannot tell a decision from drift.

# Manual start, work, end

Part of [coga/checkouts](../SKILL.md), which owns the launched lifecycle and
which checkout each step starts in.

## Procedure

Use this when no `COGA_LAUNCH_RETURNS_CHECKOUT=1` witness is set — manual or
API sessions, megalaunch picks, exempt checkouts — and before editing in a
step whose runtime notice says launch set up no branch (manual policy, or a
control step that must exceptionally change code). The agent performs both
moves:

1. **Start check.** `git fetch origin main`, then require HEAD on `main`, a
   clean tree with Coga state included, and a successful `git merge
   --ff-only origin/main`. Launch regenerates the ignored
   `coga/.agent-skills/` view; a repo initialized before `coga init` wrote
   that ignore rule sees it as dirt — add `.agent-skills/` to
   `coga/.gitignore`, never commit it. Anything else — dirty files, another
   ticket's branch, a diverged `main` — means stop: ask the attending human,
   or `coga block` in a queue run. Do not work around an occupied checkout
   with a linked worktree, a control checkout, a stash, or a switch.
2. **Work.** Write ticket state (`branch:` under `## Dev` once created with
   `git branch <name>`, plan notes) on `main`, publish it (below), then
   switch to the feature branch and change code only; ticket edits made
   there are not published until the next sweep. A resumed branch is reused:
   switch to it and `git rebase` onto fetched `origin/main`.
3. **End.** Commit, push the branch (`git push -u origin <branch>`, or
   `--force-with-lease` after a rebase), then return:
   - `git fetch origin main`;
   - for every dirty path under the Coga roots, verify it is already on
     `origin/main` by the rules of
     [the launch boundary](../launch-boundary/SKILL.md) (`git diff --quiet origin/main -- <path>`;
     for `coga/log.md`, every added line is on `origin/main`) and discard it
     (`git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree -- <path>`). `git diff`
     skips untracked files, so compare an untracked one with
     `git show origin/main:<path> | cmp - <path>` and delete it only when
     identical;
   - `git switch main`, then `git merge --ff-only origin/main`.

   If any dirty path under the Coga roots is *not* already on `origin/main`,
   or any other path is dirty, stop and escalate. A knowledge file the sweep
   [held for merge](../../state-publication/SKILL.md#held-for-merge-on-feature-checkouts)
   belongs in the branch's commit (or redone on `main`), not discarded. Never discard unpublished
   state. Then write the step's handoff on `main` and run `coga bump`, which
   publishes it. The session leaves the checkout on `main`, clean.

## Publish pre-branch ticket edits

Writing `branch:` or plan notes on `main` does not publish them: Git carries
uncommitted edits across a branch switch. Before switching, publish those
edits strictly, naming each edited file. The recipe resolves paths against
the current directory, which launch preserves, so anchor them at the checkout
root:

```sh
coga run publish-state "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/coga/tasks/<slug>.md"
git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all
```

Exit 0 means every named file is confirmed on control; any non-zero exit
(contract in [strict publication on
demand](../../state-publication/SKILL.md#strict-publication-on-demand))
is the stop signal. Use the status check only for dirty files you did not name,
and require it to be empty before switching. Do not fall back to calling the
sweep through a `python -c` one-liner: the sweep reports publication failures
without raising, and the shell's `python` often cannot import Coga at all. If
publication fails or the tree remains dirty, stop and escalate; do not switch,
stash, or commit the ticket edit on the feature branch. The same publication applies to a
sandbox clone's `worktree:` record in the primary checkout, before starting
work in the clone.

# Reconcile work with moving main

The configured remote control branch (`origin/main` by default) is the source of
truth for shared repository state. A local checkout and the launch prompt are
snapshots; expect main to advance during a session. This applies to all agent
edits, including code, documentation, contexts, skills, workflows, tickets,
and bootstrap or ad-hoc work. A fresh launch does not guarantee a fresh handoff.

## Freshness checkpoints

Before editing, fetch current main and inspect changes relevant to the work,
including its governing instructions. Before publishing or handing off edits,
fetch again and reconcile against that tip. Read-only work needs no merge;
qualify conclusions tied to an older revision if relevant files changed.
Git-disabled or remote-less work cannot claim remote freshness; report that
limitation when handing off changes.

## Preserve both sides

Reconciliation preserves main's newer work and the still-needed local intent:

- For committed branch work, merge or rebase current main using the owning
  workflow's procedure ([code branch procedure](../SKILL.md#start-work-end)).
  Resolve straightforward conflicts yourself; a clean Git merge still needs
  inspection for changes in meaning or assumptions.
- For uncommitted edits, inspect the branch's committed changes as well as
  its staged and unstaged deltas and main's intervening changes. Preserve the
  dirty deltas in patches or file copies, including untracked files, and
  record the original branch HEAD. Verify those backups before clearing any
  dirty files. Restore tracked files and the index from the branch's own
  HEAD, merge or rebase current main, then reapply the still-needed dirty
  deltas onto the resulting branch, resolving conflicts there. Do not replace
  a feature file with main's version first: that also removes committed
  branch work which a working-tree patch does not contain.
- For a stale ticket publication or a handoff, preserve unpublished prose
  and blackboard notes before refreshing the ticket from control. Account
  for committed local intent as well as dirty edits; reconcile the intended
  changes onto control's current ticket while respecting CLI-owned lifecycle
  fields. This ticket-specific recovery is not a recipe for replacing code
  files with main's version. Never replay a transition merely because its
  publication failed; use the publication recovery described in the
  [handoff procedure](../SKILL.md#in-a-launched-session).

If any work already landed, prove that from history and content before dropping
the duplicate. Preserve the owning definition and reconcile dependent references.

## Sync a feature branch with control

Every Coga command run from a feature or detached checkout publishes the
ticket and log it changed to control and leaves those files dirty in that
checkout by design ([state publication](../../state-publication/SKILL.md#control-versus-feature-checkouts)).
A new ticket stays untracked. That dirt blocks `git merge` or `git rebase` of
control until it is dropped.

Drop it only when every dirty or untracked file under the Coga and contexts
roots already equals control. Each such file must be a regular file whose
bytes (after clean filters) and mode equal the copy in the local
`<remote>/<control>` ref. A tracked file must also have no staged change.
`coga status` checks this against local refs (fetch first for a current
answer). When it holds, `coga status` prints the exact command, anchored to
the Git root, with paths quoted for the current shell. On POSIX it has this
shape, and any part with no paths is left out:

```bash
git --literal-pathspecs -C <root> checkout -- <tracked…> && rm -- <untracked…> && git -C <root> merge --no-edit <remote>/<control>
```

Native Windows PowerShell gets the same steps with `Remove-Item -LiteralPath`,
each nested in `if ($?) { … }`. `git merge --autostash` is not enough: it sets
aside tracked dirt, but an untracked ticket identical to control still aborts
the merge ("untracked working tree files would be overwritten"). Prefer merge
over rebase for a branch that is already pushed, so it needs no force-push.

When `coga status` instead lists files that differ, are staged, have another
mode, or are deleted, do not use the command. Publish differing routine state
(tickets, the log) first (`coga run publish-state`), then check again. A file
[held for merge](../../state-publication/SKILL.md#held-for-merge-on-feature-checkouts)
cannot be published from the branch: commit it on the branch for review, or
redo it on control. Otherwise reconcile those files by hand as in
[Preserve both sides](#preserve-both-sides).

## Verify and escalate

Inspect the combined diff and run checks appropriate to the affected work
after reconciliation. If publication reports that main moved again, repeat
the comparison against the new tip. Normal movement is not itself a blocker.
Escalate per session conduct when intent conflicts, ownership is unclear, or
access prevents reconciliation; identify the conflicting changes and the
decision or capability needed. Never choose main's entire file blindly,
discard unique work to silence sync, or bypass a publication or lifecycle
guard. These rules do not authorize taking over another task's dirty checkout
or crossing a human approval gate.

# Where knowledge lives

Every fact has exactly one owning file; when two copies disagree, the owner
is right. Choose the owner by what the knowledge is:

| Knowledge | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| Shared facts and contracts: behavior, invariants, edge cases, product intent used across capabilities | a local topic under the configured contexts root (`<ref>/SKILL.md`), or the package owner of a shipped topic |
| Reusable process: how to do a thing | a skill (`coga/skills/<ref>/SKILL.md` or bundled) |
| One ticket-defined capability's behavior and procedure | its command ticket (`bootstrap/<name>/ticket.md`) or recurring template (`recurring/<name>/ticket.md`) |
| Maintenance procedures specific to that capability | supporting files beside its persistent ticket, linked for reading when needed |
| Per-ticket field guide: a summary carried by new tickets that links the owning topics | inline ticket template (`src/coga/resources/ticket.md`) |
| One task's temporary working state | that ticket's blackboard ([coga/blackboard](../blackboard/SKILL.md)) |
| Execution history | `coga/log.md`, written only by CLI commands |
| Dated evidence, completed investigations, archived proposals, and other retired history | the repo's dated archive, outside the contexts root |

Humans and agents read the same owning file. Do not keep a short agent
rendition beside a longer human one: that is two owners of one fact, and the
copies drift independently. For shared facts, pick the topic whose subject
already covers the neighbouring facts; when two fit, the more narrowly
attached one wins, because the fact then costs tokens only where it is needed.

Durability alone does not make a document a context. Command tickets and
recurring templates persist; their individual executions and period tasks do
not. Keep a job's contract with the job: phone-home owns its snapshot boundary,
and Dream owns its phase order. Extract shared facts into a context and
reusable procedures into a skill when other capabilities need them.

Keep maintenance instructions separate from instructions for each run. A
template may link a sibling runbook, but recurring creation copies only
`ticket.py`, not supporting Markdown. Name the persistent template path when
directing a period to a supporting file; do not assume it is beside that
period's ticket. Skills and runbooks remain readable documentation for humans.

An owner decision *not* to act ("we looked at X and chose not to do it") is
product intent, so it belongs with X's standing owner: the shared topic, skill,
command ticket or recurring template, never only the temporary task that
recorded it. The lifecycle retires work tickets and period tasks; a decision
left in one gets re-raised. State what was declined, why, and what would reopen it.

The same retirement breaks links. Retro and `coga delete` remove a ticket
without repairing inbound references, so a topic that names a ticket by path
as the owner of an open question dangles once it retires. Point durable
surfaces at the question's standing owner, not at the transient ticket working
it, and grep for inbound references to a slug before it retires.

## Narrative links, never restates

An index, README, overview, or neighbouring topic may summarize and link to
the owner, but carries no specification-grade detail: no ordered lists, exact
names, counts or field lists that can drift on their own. "Launch stacks
conduct before task material, ticket last; the order is in
`coga/prompt-composition`" is a summary; copying the layer list is a second
specification. Command semantics live with their owning capability. A command
ticket or recurring template owns its own behavior (`bootstrap/retire/ticket.md`
owns `coga retire`); rules several jobs share stay in a topic the ticket links.
`coga/cli` is an index, and installed `coga <cmd> --help` is the syntax authority.

**Sync rule.** A PR that changes an owner greps other surfaces for the fact
and fixes or deletes any restatement in the same PR. No test enforces this
across surfaces; the authoring rule is the enforcement and Dream's knowledge
scan is the backstop. A shipped definition has one committed owner, its
package copy; a repo copy of the same ref is a deliberate local override, a
separate artifact, not a second owner to keep in sync. `CLAUDE.md` /
`AGENTS.md` load in every agent session, so they carry pointers plus only the
rules needed outside `coga launch`, never an owning statement.

## Links do not load content

Composition includes attached refs only
([coga/prompt-composition](../prompt-composition/SKILL.md)). A markdown link
in a topic, skill, or ticket is navigation: the agent reads the target only if
it chooses to open the file, subject to that repo’s access rules. So an
overview does not bring in its children. Knowledge a step requires must be
attached explicitly by ref or named as a required read in the task or skill;
a navigation link alone does neither.

## Attach or cite

Choose from the two audiences defined in
[context layout](../context-layout/SKILL.md#context-audiences): user topics
under `coga/` support operating Coga in adopting repos; the local
Coga-dev set supports developing Coga itself. Select by the task's need,
then apply the attach-or-cite test below. A shipped instruction must resolve
its required knowledge from the user set; a development link is optional
navigation, never a dependency.

For a job-owned contract or supporting file, name its persistent path and the
sections to read in the task's `## Context`. Invoke a reusable skill by ref.
Do not recreate either as a context just to put it in `contexts:`.

`contexts:` is one ticket-wide list, composed whole into every launch of
every step. Decide per ticket across all planned steps:

- **Attach** when a step must have the facts without being told to look:
  its correctness depends on rules spread across the topic, or the author
  cannot predict which facts it will hit. Test: would a launched step go
  wrong if this were absent from the prompt?
- **Cite** when steps need a few identifiable facts from a topic that is
  large relative to the rest of the prompt, or when the ticket will *edit*
  that topic (it gets read first anyway).

Measure relative size at authoring time with `approx_tokens` from
`coga launch --prompt-report`, which skips the state sweep, so a trial
`contexts:` edit stays local; do not edit lifecycle frontmatter to measure,
and do not quote sizes (they go stale). No topic is
always-attach or always-cite.

A cite is one sentence in `## Context` naming the ref and path, saying it is
cited rather than attached, and naming the sections to read, followed by the
facts the step needs, cited as module plus symbol. Do not justify it by size.
The copied facts are a snapshot for that ticket, never a second owner. Citing
does not relax the sync rule: a ticket that changes behavior a cited topic
owns updates that topic and its dependent references in the same PR.

## Topic size review policy

Each topic is a directory holding `SKILL.md` with only `name` and a
one-sentence `description` stating its scope. Targets: 60 to 160 lines and
500 to 1,500 tokens (ceil(chars/4), frontmatter included); overview topics at
most 1,000 tokens. A topic over 200 lines, 10,000 bytes, or 2,500 tokens is
reviewed for a split into narrower leaves in its namespace, so tickets can
attach only the contract they need. An exception needs a recorded reason,
written in the oversized topic itself as one closing `Size exception:`
sentence saying why it stays whole. A reason kept only on a ticket
blackboard or in a PR leaves with them, and the next reader who measures the
topic cannot tell a decision from drift.

---
name: code/with-review
description: Code change implemented by the main agent, then reviewed by its configured peer before a PR is opened for the human's final review.
steps:
  - name: implement
    assignee: agent
    requires: branch
    checkout: create-or-reuse
    skills:
      - code/implement
  - name: peer-review
    assignee: other-agent
    checkout: reuse-required
    skills:
      - code/peer-review
  - name: open-pr
    assignee: agent
    requires: pr
    checkout: control
    skills:
      - code/open-pr
  - name: review
    assignee: owner
    checkout: reuse-required
    skills:
      - code/address-pr-comments
---

## Before choosing this workflow

This workflow needs a second agent to review the code. Check `[agents.*]` in
`coga/coga.toml` and `coga.local.toml`. If only one agent is configured — or
three or more with no `peer =` on the main agent — use `code/with-self-review`
instead.

A step that declares `skills:` does **not** compose the `## <step>` section
below: Coga builds that step-specific layer from the declared skill files, and
the inline section is never read by the launched agent. The base prompt,
contexts, ticket-level skills, ticket body, and blackboard still compose
normally. Agent instructions therefore belong in the step's skills. Sections
here for a skilled step are human-facing framing only. Skill-less steps *do*
compose their section, so those bodies are load-bearing.

## Peer review by the other agent

The `implement` step derives its operator from the ticket's `agent:` main-agent
choice. The `peer-review` step declares `assignee: other-agent`, which resolves
to that main agent's configured peer. `coga bump` advances `step:` and the next
operator is derived from the frozen role; it never writes an assignment.
`open-pr` declares `agent` and routes back to the same main-agent choice.

With two configured agent types, `other-agent` infers the only peer with no
extra config. With three or more, set `peer = "<type>"` on the main agent's
`[agents.<type>]` table; the mapping is one-directional, so each main agent that
uses this workflow needs its own peer. An absent or ambiguous peer fails loud
rather than guessing.

An explicit launch override changes the executing agent without changing the
stored main agent or its peer. It can therefore make the same agent implement
and review a change. Peer selection alone does not prove independent authorship.

The `coga launch` supervisor auto-chains across these agent boundaries:
when a bump changes the derived operator (main → peer → main),
it launches the *next* agent as a fresh process under
the same supervisor — claude's REPL exits and codex's starts, or vice
versa. Each step is a clean session with a freshly composed prompt; it
only returns control to the human at the final `review` step (an
owner/human handoff), or on a terminal (`done`/`canceled`), `paused`, or
`blocked` state.

## implement

Agent step, owned by the `code/implement` skill. Launch creates or reuses the
recorded branch before the agent starts (`coga/checkouts`). The step declares
`requires: branch`, so `coga bump` refuses to advance until `branch:` is
recorded under `## Dev` in the ticket copy of the checkout the bump runs from.

## peer-review

Other-agent step, owned by the `code/peer-review` skill: the main agent's
configured peer reviews the branch diff, applies must-fix findings, freshens
the branch, and prepares `## PR` before the mechanical `open-pr` step.

Older frozen snapshots of this workflow declare no step skill, so they compose
this section instead. In that case, read and follow the `code/peer-review`
skill — `coga/skills/code/peer-review/SKILL.md` when present, else the
installed bundled copy — as if it were composed here. Peer selection alone
does not prove independent authorship; that skill says what to record.

## open-pr

Agent step, owned by the `code/open-pr` skill: `coga open-pr <slug>` pushes the
recorded branch, opens (or readies) the PR, and writes `pr:` back under
`## Dev`. It declares `requires: pr`, so `coga bump` holds the step until that
line exists.

The command is deterministic and has no judgment of its own, which is why the
preceding `peer-review` step is the one that authors the PR body and rebases the
branch.

## review

Owner-controlled gate. The human reviews the open PR on GitHub; the peer-review
pass has already applied its must-fix findings, so the diff is the post-review
state. The human decides whether to edit, request changes, push fixes, or merge.
An agent launched to assist here runs the `code/address-pr-comments` skill,
which carries the do-not-merge and do-not-bump rules for that assist.

After the human merges, the `autoclose-merged` recurring sweep marks the task
`done` on its next run (≤24h); `coga bump` closes it immediately.

`done` is not the end of the ticket. When the sweep closes it, the sweep also
disposes of the feature branch (and any leftover recorded worktree) recorded
under `## Dev`, but only what the shared checkout proofs show is safe to
remove; a `coga bump` close disposes of nothing. The closing act is still the
owner's — once the ticket is `done`, run `coga retire <slug>`. Retire runs the
same proofs on whatever checkout remains, then deletes the done ticket with no
agent: its learning already landed with the merged PR. The packaged
`bootstrap/retire/ticket.md` owns that procedure, and the
`coga/checkout-cleanup` context owns what the shared proofs prove, preserve,
and record for later sweeps.

# Maps a coga name (the token used in a ticket's `owner` / `watchers`
# fields) to a Slack member ID. With a mapping, that person gets a real
# `<@…>` ping on every post about their ticket — owners inline, watchers
# cc'd. Without one they're still named, just in plain text (no ping).
# An incoming webhook can't look an ID up itself, so it has to be listed
# here. Grab an ID from Slack: profile → ⋮ (More) → Copy member ID.
[notification.slack.users]
nicktoper = "U0AG1BASFJ7"
zach = "U0AG5LKCK8E"

# --- Git sync ---
# The git analogue of Slack: every command that mutates ticket state commits
# the resolved task directory under `coga/tasks/` and pushes it to the
# control branch, so the git-backed repo never drifts from the team's live state.
# Always-on — these defaults apply even with no `[git]` table below.
#
# When HEAD is the control branch the task files are committed and pushed; on
# a feature branch (or detached HEAD) the same files are landed on the control
# branch via a working-tree-free plumbing path. A failed commit/push is
# non-fatal: it is surfaced to stderr + the task's log.md, but never aborts the
# local state transition (the on-disk markdown is the source of truth; git is
# only the sync layer, so a push that can't reach a protected/remote control
# branch must not block a `bump` / `mark` / launch).
#
# Defaults: enabled = true, remote = "origin", control_branch = "main".
# To opt out (a repo with no remote: dev/test, CI, solo branches), set
# `enabled = false` here or in coga.local.toml (local overrides shared,
# like [notification.slack]).
#   [git]
#   enabled = true
#   remote = "origin"
#   control_branch = "main"

# --- Aliases ---
# Thin sugar over often-used commands (typically bootstrap-ticket launches).
# Aliases forward positional args after the alias name to the expanded form.

[aliases]
chat = "launch bootstrap/orient"
# `build` launches the packaged `coga-build` onboarding ticket — the same path
# `coga launch coga-build` takes. Requires an already-init'd repo.
build = "launch coga-build"
# `pick` opens the interactive megalaunch picker — a memorable name for
# `coga megalaunch --pick` (a trailing directory scopes it: `coga pick mktg`).
pick = "megalaunch --pick"
claude = "launch bootstrap/orient --agent claude"
codex = "launch bootstrap/orient --agent codex"

[layout]
# Contexts live in the docs library, anchored at the checkout root. See
# docs/archive/context-migration.md for the cutover record.
contexts = "docs/contexts"

[agents.codex]
cli = "codex"
file = "AGENTS.md"
mode = "local"
peer = "claude"
launch_args = "--no-daemon -m gpt-6.1-sol -c model_reasoning_effort=\"medium\" -a never -c 'permissions.trial.filesystem={\":root\"=\"read\",\":slash_tmp\"=\"write\",\"/tmp/coga-quality-trial/.git\"=\"write\"}' -c permissions.trial.network.enabled=true -c 'default_permissions=\"trial\"' -c 'projects.\"/tmp/coga-quality-trial\".trust_level=\"trusted\"'"
discussion = "-c developer_instructions={prompt}"

# Trial: the peer exists only so `other-agent` resolves; its CLI is absent, so
# the launch supervisor stops after the one measured step instead of chaining.
[agents.claude]
cli = "claude-absent-in-trial"
file = "CLAUDE.md"
mode = "local"

[telemetry]
enabled = false
---
name: code/with-review
description: Code change implemented by the main agent, then reviewed by its configured peer before a PR is opened for the human's final review.
steps:
  - name: implement
    assignee: agent
    requires: branch
    checkout: create-or-reuse
    skills:
      - code/implement
  - name: peer-review
    assignee: other-agent
    checkout: reuse-required
    skills:
      - code/peer-review
  - name: open-pr
    assignee: agent
    requires: pr
    checkout: control
    skills:
      - code/open-pr
  - name: review
    assignee: owner
    checkout: reuse-required
    skills:
      - code/address-pr-comments
---

## Before choosing this workflow

This workflow needs a second agent to review the code. Check `[agents.*]` in
`coga/coga.toml` and `coga.local.toml`. If only one agent is configured — or
three or more with no `peer =` on the main agent — use `code/with-self-review`
instead.

A step that declares `skills:` does **not** compose the `## <step>` section
below: Coga builds that step-specific layer from the declared skill files, and
the inline section is never read by the launched agent. The base prompt,
contexts, ticket-level skills, ticket body, and blackboard still compose
normally. Agent instructions therefore belong in the step's skills. Sections
here for a skilled step are human-facing framing only. Skill-less steps *do*
compose their section, so those bodies are load-bearing.

## Peer review by the other agent

The `implement` step derives its operator from the ticket's `agent:` main-agent
choice. The `peer-review` step declares `assignee: other-agent`, which resolves
to that main agent's configured peer. `coga bump` advances `step:` and the next
operator is derived from the frozen role; it never writes an assignment.
`open-pr` declares `agent` and routes back to the same main-agent choice.

With two configured agent types, `other-agent` infers the only peer with no
extra config. With three or more, set `peer = "<type>"` on the main agent's
`[agents.<type>]` table; the mapping is one-directional, so each main agent that
uses this workflow needs its own peer. An absent or ambiguous peer fails loud
rather than guessing.

An explicit launch override changes the executing agent without changing the
stored main agent or its peer. It can therefore make the same agent implement
and review a change. Peer selection alone does not prove independent authorship.

The `coga launch` supervisor auto-chains across these agent boundaries:
when a bump changes the derived operator (main → peer → main),
it launches the *next* agent as a fresh process under
the same supervisor — claude's REPL exits and codex's starts, or vice
versa. Each step is a clean session with a freshly composed prompt; it
only returns control to the human at the final `review` step (an
owner/human handoff), or on a terminal (`done`/`canceled`), `paused`, or
`blocked` state.

## implement

Agent step, owned by the `code/implement` skill. Launch creates or reuses the
recorded branch before the agent starts (`coga/checkouts`). The step declares
`requires: branch`, so `coga bump` refuses to advance until `branch:` is
recorded under `## Dev` in the ticket copy of the checkout the bump runs from.

## peer-review

Other-agent step, owned by the `code/peer-review` skill: the main agent's
configured peer reviews the branch diff, applies must-fix findings, freshens
the branch, and prepares `## PR` before the mechanical `open-pr` step.

Older frozen snapshots of this workflow declare no step skill, so they compose
this section instead. In that case, read and follow the `code/peer-review`
skill — `coga/skills/code/peer-review/SKILL.md` when present, else the
installed bundled copy — as if it were composed here. Peer selection alone
does not prove independent authorship; that skill says what to record.

## open-pr

Agent step, owned by the `code/open-pr` skill: `coga open-pr <slug>` pushes the
recorded branch, opens (or readies) the PR, and writes `pr:` back under
`## Dev`. It declares `requires: pr`, so `coga bump` holds the step until that
line exists.

The command is deterministic and has no judgment of its own, which is why the
preceding `peer-review` step is the one that authors the PR body and rebases the
branch.

## review

Owner-controlled gate. The human reviews the open PR on GitHub; the peer-review
pass has already applied its must-fix findings, so the diff is the post-review
state. The human decides whether to edit, request changes, push fixes, or merge.
An agent launched to assist here runs the `code/address-pr-comments` skill,
which carries the do-not-merge and do-not-bump rules for that assist.

After the human merges, the `autoclose-merged` recurring sweep marks the task
`done` on its next run (≤24h); `coga bump` closes it immediately.

`done` is not the end of the ticket. When the sweep closes it, the sweep also
disposes of the feature branch (and any leftover recorded worktree) recorded
under `## Dev`, but only what the shared checkout proofs show is safe to
remove; a `coga bump` close disposes of nothing. The closing act is still the
owner's — once the ticket is `done`, run `coga retire <slug>`. Retire runs the
same proofs on whatever checkout remains, then deletes the done ticket with no
agent: its learning already landed with the merged PR. The packaged
`bootstrap/retire/ticket.md` owns that procedure, and the
`coga/checkout-cleanup` context owns what the shared proofs prove, preserve,
and record for later sweeps.
"}

# Coga documentation

The [project README](../README.md) explains what Coga is and shows the
workflow. This index is for finding the details: using Coga in a repository,
understanding its files and commands, or contributing to Coga itself.

## Start

1. [Get started](../README.md#get-started) — install Coga and check prerequisites.
2. [Set up a repo](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/init/SKILL.md) — fresh, or a clone already using Coga.
3. [Take a first task](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/first-task/SKILL.md) from draft to PR.
4. [Remove Coga](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/uninstall/SKILL.md) if you need to.

The project README's Get started section is the only install path. The
native Windows boundary is in
[coga/launch](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/launch/SKILL.md#options-and-exits).

## Understand

Coga keeps work readable and editable across agent sessions. Its
[building blocks](../README.md#what-lives-in-your-repo) are
[tickets](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/tickets/SKILL.md) for units of work,
[contexts](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/knowledge/SKILL.md) for lasting knowledge,
[workflows](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/workflows/SKILL.md) for steps and review gates,
and [history](../coga/log.md) for recorded transitions.

- [Architecture](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/architecture/SKILL.md) — the model and the
  correction loop.
- Working with tickets: [discovery](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/tickets/discovery/SKILL.md),
  [authoring](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/tickets/authoring/SKILL.md),
  [lifecycle](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/lifecycle/SKILL.md), and
  [blackboard](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/blackboard/SKILL.md).
- [Prompt composition](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/prompt-composition/SKILL.md) — what an
  agent receives; [knowledge placement](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/knowledge/SKILL.md) —
  which context belongs with a task.
- The [annotated ticket template](../src/coga/resources/ticket.md) explains
  the fields in new tickets.

## Operate

- Commands: the [CLI index](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/cli/SKILL.md) points each command
  at its owning topic.
- Configuration: [coga.toml and local config](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/configuration/SKILL.md),
  [directory layout](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/context-layout/SKILL.md),
  [secrets](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/secrets/SKILL.md).
- Running work: [launch](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/launch/SKILL.md),
  [script tickets](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/script-tickets/SKILL.md),
  [megalaunch queue](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/megalaunch/SKILL.md).
- Recurring jobs: [overview](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/recurring/SKILL.md),
  [templates](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/recurring/templates/SKILL.md),
  [scheduling](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/recurring/scheduling/SKILL.md)
  ([inactivity](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/recurring/scheduling/inactivity/SKILL.md)),
  [delegation](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/recurring/delegation/SKILL.md),
  [autofix](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/recurring/autofix/SKILL.md),
  [period tasks](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/period-task/SKILL.md),
  [Dream](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/recurring/dream/ticket.md).
- Team sync: [Git state overview](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/sync/SKILL.md),
  [notifications](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/notifications/SKILL.md)
  ([producers](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/notifications/producers/SKILL.md)),
  [coga-important](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/important/SKILL.md), and
  [usage records](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/usage/SKILL.md).

- Publication: [PRs](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/pr-publication/SKILL.md)
  ([preparation](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/pr-publication/preparation/SKILL.md));
  [human assists](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/human-assist/SKILL.md);
  [state publication and recovery](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/state-publication/SKILL.md).
- Extending and recovering a repo: [extension choices](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/extension-model/SKILL.md),
  [edge code and forks](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/edge-code/SKILL.md),
  [agent sandboxes](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/sandboxes/SKILL.md).

- Code-task conventions: [checkouts](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/checkouts/SKILL.md)
  ([launch boundary](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/checkouts/launch-boundary/SKILL.md),
  [sandbox clone](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/checkouts/sandbox-clone/SKILL.md)),
  [design history](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/blackboard/SKILL.md#superseded-designs),
  [checkout cleanup](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/checkout-cleanup/SKILL.md)
  ([terminal owners](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/checkout-cleanup/terminal-owners/SKILL.md),
  [branch sweep](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/checkout-cleanup/branch-sweep/SKILL.md)).

## Develop Coga

If you want to change Coga, start with [Contributing](../CONTRIBUTING.md).
The local-only Coga-dev topics and maintainer skills cover implementation:

- [Design principles](contexts/coga-dev/principles/SKILL.md),
  [patterns](contexts/coga-dev/patterns/SKILL.md), and the
  [microkernel boundary](contexts/coga-dev/microkernel/SKILL.md).
- [Internals index](contexts/coga-dev/internals/SKILL.md) for concurrency,
  publication transactions, recurring admission, and activity capture.
- [Codebase](contexts/coga-dev/codebase/SKILL.md) source map and
  [gotchas](contexts/coga-dev/codebase/gotchas/SKILL.md).
- [Weekly telemetry](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/recurring/phone-home/ticket.md) (opt-out) and its
  [operator runbook](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/recurring/phone-home/operations.md) for release
  verification, read-back and deletion.
- [Testing](contexts/coga-dev/testing/SKILL.md) and the clean-install skills
  ([Linux](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/skills/coga/testing/clean-install/SKILL.md),
  [macOS on AWS](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/skills/coga/testing/clean-install/macos-aws/SKILL.md),
  [Windows on AWS](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/skills/coga/testing/clean-install/windows-aws/SKILL.md),
  [attended human walk](../coga/skills/coga/testing/clean-install/human-walk/SKILL.md)
  on a [fresh VM](../coga/skills/coga/testing/fresh-vm/SKILL.md)),
  [packaging](contexts/coga-dev/packaging/SKILL.md),
  [release skill](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/skills/coga/releasing/SKILL.md).
- This repo's posture (dated, local to this repo):
  [current direction](contexts/coga-dev/current-direction/SKILL.md),
  [project stage](contexts/coga-dev/project-stage/SKILL.md).

## How this library works

The same Markdown topics are read by people and can be attached to agents'
prompts. A ticket attaches a
context by its ref (for example, `contexts: [coga/launch]`); a Markdown
link is only navigation and does **not** load that topic into the prompt.

There are two audiences. [User topics](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/) under `coga/`
describe what an adopting repository needs to run Coga and ship as packaged
fallbacks. [Coga-dev topics](contexts/coga-dev/) under `coga-dev/`
describe Coga's implementation and stay in this source repository.
[Context layout](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/context-layout/SKILL.md#context-audiences)
defines the boundary; [knowledge placement](../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/knowledge/SKILL.md)
defines where facts belong. For older context refs, see the
[migration note](release-notes/context-audiences.md). Shipped definitions are
owned by the package and resolved local-first; the
[package-definitions note](release-notes/package-definitions.md) covers
recurring selection, state carriers and migrating an existing repo. This
source repo uses those package owners directly; there is no second user-topic
tree under `docs/contexts/`. Its local topics are the Coga-dev library above.

## Proposals and history

These are historical documents, **not current instructions**. Dated evidence
and earlier decisions can be useful, but agents must not read or search the
archive without an explicit human request
([archive access rule](contexts/coga-dev/archive-access/SKILL.md#archive-access)).

- [Archived evidence](archive/evidence/) — dated investigations, comparisons,
  and test results.
- [Archived designs](archive/design/) — proposals that may never have shipped.
- [Other history](archive/) — origins, prior positioning, migrations, and
  retired plans; see the [superseded decisions](archive/superseded-decisions.md)
  and [context migration record](archive/context-migration.md) for those topics.

name: coga/tickets/discovery
description: Where tickets live and how they are named — task discovery, file versus directory form, parked and group directories, task refs, finding a retired task in Git, and the reserved `ticket.py` sibling.
---

# Where tasks live and how they are named

Part of [coga/tickets](../SKILL.md).

Discovery walks `coga/tasks/` at any depth:

- **Directory form**: a directory holding `ticket.md`, plus any attachments.
  A task directory is never recursed into (no task inside a task).
- **File form**: a bare `tasks/<slug>.md`, for a self-contained task with no
  siblings. Promote with `mkdir <slug>/ && mv <slug>.md <slug>/ticket.md`.
- `<slug>.md` and `<slug>/` must not both exist.
- `README.md` is never a task; it documents its directory. Names starting
  with `_` are skipped at every level: `_template` is reserved (below), and
  any other `_`-prefixed directory is **parked**.
- A **parked** directory (such as `_v2/`) keeps files Coga never lists,
  launches, validates, or scans for Dream, while state sync still publishes
  them. It holds captures and wishes that need not be current or consistent.
  `coga create "_v2/<title>"` writes there, title-only is fine, and `coga
  ticket` refuses a parked target. `_template` is reserved at every level:
  `coga/.gitignore` ignores it, so `coga create` refuses it as a component. Pull an item forward with `git mv` out of
  the parked tree; it is then an ordinary ticket and must pass validation.
- Other directories are plain folders managed with `mkdir`/`mv`/`rm`; Coga
  has no command for them.
- **The directory is the group.** Related tickets sit side by side in a plain
  folder whose `README.md` holds shared material; the folder has no workflow,
  status, owner, or completion. There is no parent or umbrella ticket: when
  splitting work, give every deliverable to a real sibling ticket, then remove
  the original with `coga delete` rather than keeping it as a parent
  (`coga retire` accepts only a `done` or `canceled` ticket). Pick a group path other than
  the original's own path: `coga create` refuses to nest a ticket inside a
  directory-form task. Do not put `ticket.md` at a group root; that makes it a
  task, and discovery stops there. Coga deliberately has no split contract
  (no split skill, roster section, or cross-link convention): agents rarely
  used the added instructions, so they were prompt noise. Reopen only on
  evidence of repeated oversized-ticket failures.

A task's identity is its **path under `tasks/`**: the bare leaf at top level,
otherwise the relative path (`marketing/social/relaunch`). Refs and log tags
use forward slashes on every platform, including native Windows. A ref resolves when
it is an exact ref or a unique prefix; a nested task's bare leaf does not
resolve, and ambiguous prefixes fail listing the matches. Agents use the exact
task directory printed in the composed prompt header rather than rebuilding it
from the ref. Log lines are tagged with the ref and never rewritten, so moving
a task orphans its history under the old tag: record the prior ref in the body
and grep for it.

A retired or deleted task (`coga retire`, `delete-task`, Retro) leaves its
body and blackboard only as a Git blob; `coga show` no longer finds it. Find
the deleting commit on the control ref, then read the file from its parent.
`<control>` is `<remote>/<control_branch>` from `coga.toml` `[git]`
([coga/configuration](../../configuration/SKILL.md) owns the keys and defaults),
or the local `<control_branch>` in a repo with no remote:

```bash
git log <control> --diff-filter=D --name-only -- \
  ':(glob)coga/tasks/**/<slug>.md' ':(glob)coga/tasks/**/<slug>/**'
git show <commit>^:<path>
```

The pathspecs name the slug exactly, in both the `<slug>.md` and `<slug>/`
forms at any group depth, so a task whose slug merely starts with `<slug>` is
not matched. The newest hit that deletes `<slug>.md` or
`<slug>/ticket.md` is the retirement; older hits are a `.md` ↔ `<slug>/`
format conversion or an attachment removed earlier. Older directory-form
tasks kept the blackboard in a sibling `blackboard.md`; read it the same way.

A directory-form task may reserve the exact sibling `ticket.py` as its
deterministic phase ([coga/script-tickets](../../script-tickets/SKILL.md)); no
other attachment changes dispatch. Attachments are never composed.

name: coga/configuration
description: The shared `coga.toml` versus machine-local `coga.local.toml` split, each file's key allowlist, fail-loud unknown-key and migration errors, and where `env:` indirection works.
---

# Configuration

Coga reads two files from the Coga root:

- **`coga.toml`**, committed: repo policy every clone must agree on.
- **`coga.local.toml`**, gitignored: facts about this machine and operator.
  `COGA_LOCAL_CONFIG` can point a process at an absolute path instead, so a
  Coga process in another checkout of the same repo, such as a relay
  worktree, reads the operator's local settings.

Both are validated against fixed schemas on every command that loads config.
Two invocations read neither file, so neither validates config nor sweeps
state: `coga --version`, and `--help`/`-h` under a built-in command (for
example `coga launch --help`). Top-level `coga --help`
still loads config to list the repo's `[aliases]`. Never commit real
credentials. Use indirection ([coga/secrets](../secrets/SKILL.md)).

## Choosing an agent

Init declares the agents whose CLI it found on `PATH` and comments out the
`[agents.*]` table of every other supported agent. So with one agent installed
you need no config edit: that agent is the only declared type and therefore the
default. To add another, install its CLI and uncomment its table in
`coga/coga.toml`.

In a repo that declares both, choose which one new tasks get with this
top-level setting, placed before any `[table]` in `coga/coga.local.toml`:

```toml
default_agent = "codex"
```

This does not change an already activated ticket or select the interviewer
for `coga chat` and `coga ticket`. Use `coga chat --agent codex` or
`coga ticket "Your task title" --agent codex` for those sessions.

One limit to know in a repo that declares Codex but not Claude Code. The
packaged `coga chat` and `coga ticket` tickets pin `agent: claude`, and a
`--agent` override cannot repair a pin that names an undeclared type, so
`coga chat` fails there even with `--agent codex`; `coga ticket --agent codex`
works, because authoring checks the override first. `coga build` works, because
init points its ticket at the agent it found. Uncommenting `[agents.claude]`
gets `coga chat` past that routing check, since the pin is a name matched
against this file — but the session then needs the `claude` binary like any
other launch. Making those commands agent-agnostic is the real fix and is
tracked separately.

The comments beside `default_agent` and `[agents.*]` in the
[shipped configuration](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/coga.toml)
own precedence and routing details. Workflow roles and peer selection are
explained in [coga/workflows](../workflows/SKILL.md); the
[first-task walk](../first-task/SKILL.md) covers the prerequisites for a PR
with either one agent or a peer reviewer.

## Allowlists

`coga.toml` top level: `version` (must be `1`), `default_status`,
`default_agent`, `owner`, `agents`, `notification`, `git`, `launch`, `ticket`, `aliases`,
`extensions`, `layout`, `autofix`, `telemetry`, `recurring`, `log`.

`coga.local.toml` top level: `user`, `default_agent`, `agents`,
`notification`, `git`, `upstream`, `telemetry`, `authoring`.

`default_agent` is a string in both files. The local value wins, and each
present value must name a type in the merged `[agents.*]`; it is validated at
load. Precedence, freezing at activation, and what it does not move are
explained beside the key in the shipped `coga.toml`.

| Table | Keys | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `[agents.<name>]` | `cli`, `file` (both required), `mode`, `name_flag`, `session_id_flag`, `launch_args`, `discussion`, `analyze`, `peer` | both; local overlays shared key by key (explained in the shipped `coga.toml`) |
| `[notification]` | `channels`, `slack` | both |
| `[notification.slack]` | `webhook`, `important_webhook`, `enabled`, `gifs`, `users` | both; local wins ([coga/notifications](../notifications/SKILL.md)) |
| `[git]` | `enabled`, `remote`, `control_branch`, `worktrees_ticket_owned` | shared |
| `[git]` | `enabled` only | local; overrides shared ([coga/state-publication](../state-publication/SKILL.md)) |
| `[log]` | `retention_days` (non-negative integer, default `30`; `0` disables trimming) | shared only |
| `[recurring]` | `idle_days` (non-negative integer, default `14`; `0` disables inactivity gating) | shared only |
| `[launch]` | `idle_timeout`, `max_session` | shared |
| `[ticket]` / `[ticket.fields.<name>]` | `fields` / `description`, `values`, `default`, `required` | shared ([coga/tickets](../tickets/SKILL.md)) |
| `[layout]` | `contexts` | shared only ([coga/context-layout](../context-layout/SKILL.md)) |
| `[autofix]` | `agent`, `contexts` | shared only ([coga/recurring/autofix](../recurring/autofix/SKILL.md)) |
| `[upstream]` | `checkouts` | local only |
| `[authoring]` | `agent` | local only ([coga/tickets/authoring](../tickets/authoring/SKILL.md)) |
| `[telemetry]` | `enabled` (boolean only) | both; local overrides shared, including local true over shared false |

The split is deliberate. `[layout]` and `[autofix]` are team policy: one
clone must not resolve a context ref somewhere another clone does not.
`[upstream] checkouts` is the mirror image. It names absolute paths to other
repos on this machine, so it is accepted only locally and validated for
shape alone: a list of non-empty strings, `~` expanded, required to be
absolute. A path missing on disk still loads and is skipped by its consumer,
because failing config load would brick every command when a client repo
moves. `[authoring] agent` is local for the same reason: which agent an
operator authors tickets with (say, while one agent's quota is exhausted) is
a fact about that operator. Load checks only its shape; the name is checked
against `[agents]` when authoring resolves it, and `COGA_AUTHORING_AGENT`
overrides it. `user` is always local and never guessed
([coga/init](../init/SKILL.md)).

## Unknown keys fail loud

Any unrecognized key at any level of a fixed-schema table, in either file,
raises `ConfigError` naming the offender and listing the allowed keys. A
misspelled `[notification.slak]` therefore stops every config-loading command
instead of silently resolving to "no webhook".

Free-form maps are exempt because their keys are data: `[aliases]`,
`[extensions]` (a repo-owned namespace Coga passes through uninterpreted),
`[notification.slack.gifs]`, and `[notification.slack.users]`.

Known-but-removed or misplaced keys raise tailored errors **before** the
generic check, so the actionable message survives:

- `[assignees]` and `[megalaunch]` in `coga.toml`;
- `[secrets]` in `coga.local.toml` (secrets are declared inline on tickets);
- `[authoring]` in `coga.toml` (machine-local; the install-level default is
  `bootstrap/ticket`'s `agent:`);
- `[slack]` in either file (moved under `[notification.slack]`);
- `auto`, `skip_permissions`, `skip_permissions_argv` in any
  `[agents.<name>]`, reported against the file that contains them.

## `env:` indirection in config

Config values are otherwise literal. Exactly two fields run an `env:VAR`
reference through the shared resolver: `[notification.slack].webhook` and
`[notification.slack].important_webhook`. An unset
variable there resolves to "no webhook configured". An `env:VAR` written in
any other config field is a literal string, not an indirection, and `op://`
is not understood anywhere in config. Ticket `secrets:` are a separate,
fail-loud path.

## Other configuration surfaces

`owner` (the recurring operator), `[launch]` limits, and `[autofix]` are
owned by [coga/recurring](../recurring/SKILL.md). `[aliases]` expand to
Coga argv ([coga/cli](../cli/SKILL.md)).

Telemetry defaults on. Both `[telemetry]` layers are
validated even when overridden. No endpoint, key, cadence, or test bypass is
configurable. Delivery, state and payload belong to
[phone-home ticket](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/recurring/phone-home/ticket.md); git and notification switches remain
independent.

`[recurring].idle_days` is team policy and cannot be overridden locally.
Booleans, negative values and non-integers raise `ConfigError`. The activity
signal, calendar boundary and sweep overrides are owned by
[recurring scheduling](../recurring/scheduling/inactivity/SKILL.md).

`[log].retention_days` cannot be overridden locally. Booleans, negative values,
non-integers, non-table values and unknown keys fail config loading. Very large
positive integers saturate at `datetime.min` when computing the cutoff. Days
are local calendar days, matching timezone-free log envelopes: complete
unprotected events strictly before local midnight on today minus the window
expire. The boundary and future timestamps stay. The
[trim-log ticket](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/recurring/trim-log/ticket.md)
owns exceptions and its weekly schedule; its
[operations guide](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/recurring/trim-log/operations.md)
owns default-on adoption for existing repos.
