name: coga/blackboard
description: The writer's contract for a ticket blackboard — locating the fence, scoping edits, live sections and superseded designs, the draft-activation readiness check, size limits and their remedy, and safe concurrent writes. Attach to tickets whose work writes blackboards programmatically.
---

# Writing to a ticket blackboard

The blackboard is everything below the `<!-- coga:blackboard -->` fence in a
ticket: working memory shared by human and agent and carried between
stateless sessions. Its live state is composed into every launch
([coga/prompt-composition](../prompt-composition/SKILL.md)); `coga/log.md`,
written only by CLI commands, holds lifecycle history and is never composed.
Working state the next run must read goes here and stays small; history goes
in the log.

## The fence

The fence counts only as a whole line: no leading indentation, optional
trailing whitespace. Markdown is not parsed, so an own-line fence inside a
code block counts, while an inline mention does not.

- **Never locate the fence by substring** (`split`, `find`, `partition`,
  unanchored `grep`/`sed`): a quoted fence in prose truncates the body.
- **Exactly one fence.** Readers fail on zero or several. Bootstrap command
  tickets legitimately have none.
- **Scope each edit.** Compute every transform on the blackboard region, never
  on whole-file text, so a `## Heading` pattern cannot hit the body, and never
  reformat the YAML while writing below the fence.

What may be edited above the fence is owned by
[coga/tickets](../tickets/SKILL.md) (agents: `contexts` and body sections).

## Section regimes

Match the section's regime; do not invent a fourth.

- **Live state: rewrite in place.** One current value per named line. `## Dev`
  (`branch:`, `worktree:`, `pr:`) is canonical; its shape is in
  the ticket template's guide comment. Old values live in git.
- **Record: append, never delete.** `## Superseded designs` takes dated
  entries (shape [below](#superseded-designs);
  only an archive pointer composes). `## Blockers` takes one checkbox per ask;
  `coga unblock` marks it `- [x]` and appends `resolved:`. Blocker readers
  ignore fenced examples and superseded sections.
  The writer does not (known limitation, unfixed): when a real ask is open,
  `coga unblock` (`blackboard.resolve_open_blockers`) also flips `- [ ]`
  examples in fences and superseded sections and appends `resolved:` to
  them, so keep example blockers out of a blackboard that may be unblocked.
- **Authoring scratch: synthesize before launch.** `## Evaluator review`,
  `## Ticket authoring notes`, `## Proposals`. The `bootstrap/ticket` cleanup
  folds durable substance into the body; for a draft it keeps
  `## Superseded designs` and resets the rest to the stock placeholder; for a
  non-draft it removes only the authoring sections it used.

## Superseded designs

When a design changes, rewrite `## Description` and `## Context` to describe
current work, with live requirements under `###` subheadings. Other top-level
body sections do not compose. Move the abandoned plan below the blackboard
fence into one `## Superseded designs` section; append dated entries oldest
to newest:

```markdown
## Superseded designs

### YYYY-MM-DD — <abandoned direction>

Superseded by: <current direction or decision>
Reason: <why the ticket pivoted>

<prior plan, acceptance details, and evidence worth retaining>
```

Retain enough to understand or reconsider the old plan, with copied headings
at `####` or deeper inside each entry. Keep history in this single section,
not scattered under alternative headings or left only in Git; only the exact,
unindented `## Superseded designs` heading starts it. The body may carry one
short pointer when a reviewer needs it; keep current decisions and their
rationale in live notes. The prompt includes only a pointer to the stored
history.

## Draft-activation readiness

On first activation (`mark active` or launch auto-activation) Coga refuses a
draft whose blackboard still holds authoring scratch sections or a large
custom scratchpad, before anything is written or spawned; `coga validate`
reports the same error. The stock placeholder (resource `blackboard.md`, which
a repo may override under `<coga root>/resources/`) counts as empty. Merge
durable requirements into `## Description` / `## Context` first. A
`## Production notes` section marks remaining content as intentional launch
material and exempts it; `## Superseded designs` is excluded without
exempting other notes. Later reactivations and forced recurring reruns do not
recheck. An `## Evaluator review` written by a live workflow step is working
state for the next owner gate, not residue.

## Size and its remedy

`coga validate` (`large-blackboard`) and launch warn above 32 KiB of live
notes. When `coga launch --prompt-report` shows the blackboard as the
largest layer, do not delete history. Promote a file-form task to directory
form, move dated evidence into sibling attachments (`tasks/<slug>/<topic>.md`,
opening with an HTML comment naming the task and move date), and leave the
current handoff, worklist and verification with a pointer to each. Keep
`## Dev` and `## Blockers` in place, since CLI readers do not follow links.
Material several tickets cite belongs in an unattached context. Record the
before/after layer sizes on the blackboard. A moved section leaves a
same-named heading holding only the pointer, so references to it (an
evaluator review citing `## Design`) still resolve.

The remedy is for live tickets. A flagged `done` ticket is not trimmed: one
with no live recorded checkout is left to Dream's retro pass, and one with a
live checkout is retirement debt that `coga retire <slug>` disposes of and
deletes ([Dream template](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/recurring/dream/ticket.md) owns that split). A section a writer rewrites
every run (a recurring template's state, Dream's own per-run report) is not
trimmed by hand either: the next run overwrites the edit, and
[coga/period-task](../period-task/SKILL.md) says to touch only your own keys.
Route it to its owner as a decision (attachment, exemption, or accepted
warning).

## Publishing cleanup

Draft synthesis and live-ticket size cleanup publish as Coga state through
[state publication](../state-publication/SKILL.md). The owner can edit directly
on control or track the cleanup in a workflow without branch or PR gates.
Ticket bodies, blackboards, and sibling attachments stay out of code PRs.

## What later passes do to content

- A replaced live value leaves the section; git keeps it.
- A replaced design moves into the single `## Superseded designs` section;
  the body keeps at most a one-line pointer. Keep rationale still needed for
  current work in live notes.
- A resolved blocker keeps its ask.
- A period task's blackboard is deleted at Dream's retro cleanup: durable
  gotchas go under `## Gotchas` for extraction and last-run state goes on the
  parent template's blackboard ([coga/period-task](../period-task/SKILL.md)).

## Concurrent writers

There is no ownership mutex; divergent workers are visible and recoverable in
git ([coga/launch](../launch/SKILL.md)). A `ticket.py` or other program that
writes a blackboard uses `blackboard.update_blackboard_under_barrier`, which
refuses rather than overwrite an intervening edit. Read the region
immediately before writing, prefer section appends to whole-region rewrites,
and keep writes as small as the change. Parser and race details are in
[blackboard IO](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/docs/contexts/coga-dev/internals/blackboard-io/SKILL.md);
cross-checkout reconciliation is in [coga/sync](../sync/SKILL.md).

# Where tasks live and how they are named

Part of [coga/tickets](../SKILL.md).

Discovery walks `coga/tasks/` at any depth:

- **Directory form**: a directory holding `ticket.md`, plus any attachments.
  A task directory is never recursed into (no task inside a task).
- **File form**: a bare `tasks/<slug>.md`, for a self-contained task with no
  siblings. Promote with `mkdir <slug>/ && mv <slug>.md <slug>/ticket.md`.
- `<slug>.md` and `<slug>/` must not both exist.
- `README.md` is never a task; it documents its directory. Names starting
  with `_` are skipped at every level: `_template` is reserved (below), and
  any other `_`-prefixed directory is **parked**.
- A **parked** directory (such as `_v2/`) keeps files Coga never lists,
  launches, validates, or scans for Dream, while state sync still publishes
  them. It holds captures and wishes that need not be current or consistent.
  `coga create "_v2/<title>"` writes there, title-only is fine, and `coga
  ticket` refuses a parked target. `_template` is reserved at every level:
  `coga/.gitignore` ignores it, so `coga create` refuses it as a component. Pull an item forward with `git mv` out of
  the parked tree; it is then an ordinary ticket and must pass validation.
- Other directories are plain folders managed with `mkdir`/`mv`/`rm`; Coga
  has no command for them.
- **The directory is the group.** Related tickets sit side by side in a plain
  folder whose `README.md` holds shared material; the folder has no workflow,
  status, owner, or completion. There is no parent or umbrella ticket: when
  splitting work, give every deliverable to a real sibling ticket, then remove
  the original with `coga delete` rather than keeping it as a parent
  (`coga retire` accepts only a `done` or `canceled` ticket). Pick a group path other than
  the original's own path: `coga create` refuses to nest a ticket inside a
  directory-form task. Do not put `ticket.md` at a group root; that makes it a
  task, and discovery stops there. Coga deliberately has no split contract
  (no split skill, roster section, or cross-link convention): agents rarely
  used the added instructions, so they were prompt noise. Reopen only on
  evidence of repeated oversized-ticket failures.

A task's identity is its **path under `tasks/`**: the bare leaf at top level,
otherwise the relative path (`marketing/social/relaunch`). Refs and log tags
use forward slashes on every platform, including native Windows. A ref resolves when
it is an exact ref or a unique prefix; a nested task's bare leaf does not
resolve, and ambiguous prefixes fail listing the matches. Agents use the exact
task directory printed in the composed prompt header rather than rebuilding it
from the ref. Log lines are tagged with the ref and never rewritten, so moving
a task orphans its history under the old tag: record the prior ref in the body
and grep for it.

A retired or deleted task (`coga retire`, `delete-task`, Retro) leaves its
body and blackboard only as a Git blob; `coga show` no longer finds it. Find
the deleting commit on the control ref, then read the file from its parent.
`<control>` is `<remote>/<control_branch>` from `coga.toml` `[git]`
([coga/configuration](../../configuration/SKILL.md) owns the keys and defaults),
or the local `<control_branch>` in a repo with no remote:

```bash
git log <control> --diff-filter=D --name-only -- \
  ':(glob)coga/tasks/**/<slug>.md' ':(glob)coga/tasks/**/<slug>/**'
git show <commit>^:<path>
```

The pathspecs name the slug exactly, in both the `<slug>.md` and `<slug>/`
forms at any group depth, so a task whose slug merely starts with `<slug>` is
not matched. The newest hit that deletes `<slug>.md` or
`<slug>/ticket.md` is the retirement; older hits are a `.md` ↔ `<slug>/`
format conversion or an attachment removed earlier. Older directory-form
tasks kept the blackboard in a sibling `blackboard.md`; read it the same way.

A directory-form task may reserve the exact sibling `ticket.py` as its
deterministic phase ([coga/script-tickets](../../script-tickets/SKILL.md)); no
other attachment changes dispatch. Attachments are never composed.

# Configuration

Coga reads two files from the Coga root:

- **`coga.toml`**, committed: repo policy every clone must agree on.
- **`coga.local.toml`**, gitignored: facts about this machine and operator.
  `COGA_LOCAL_CONFIG` can point a process at an absolute path instead, so a
  Coga process in another checkout of the same repo, such as a relay
  worktree, reads the operator's local settings.

Both are validated against fixed schemas on every command that loads config.
Two invocations read neither file, so neither validates config nor sweeps
state: `coga --version`, and `--help`/`-h` under a built-in command (for
example `coga launch --help`). Top-level `coga --help`
still loads config to list the repo's `[aliases]`. Never commit real
credentials. Use indirection ([coga/secrets](../secrets/SKILL.md)).

## Choosing an agent

Init declares the agents whose CLI it found on `PATH` and comments out the
`[agents.*]` table of every other supported agent. So with one agent installed
you need no config edit: that agent is the only declared type and therefore the
default. To add another, install its CLI and uncomment its table in
`coga/coga.toml`.

In a repo that declares both, choose which one new tasks get with this
top-level setting, placed before any `[table]` in `coga/coga.local.toml`:

```toml
default_agent = "codex"
```

This does not change an already activated ticket or select the interviewer
for `coga chat` and `coga ticket`. Use `coga chat --agent codex` or
`coga ticket "Your task title" --agent codex` for those sessions.

One limit to know in a repo that declares Codex but not Claude Code. The
packaged `coga chat` and `coga ticket` tickets pin `agent: claude`, and a
`--agent` override cannot repair a pin that names an undeclared type, so
`coga chat` fails there even with `--agent codex`; `coga ticket --agent codex`
works, because authoring checks the override first. `coga build` works, because
init points its ticket at the agent it found. Uncommenting `[agents.claude]`
gets `coga chat` past that routing check, since the pin is a name matched
against this file — but the session then needs the `claude` binary like any
other launch. Making those commands agent-agnostic is the real fix and is
tracked separately.

The comments beside `default_agent` and `[agents.*]` in the
[shipped configuration](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/coga.toml)
own precedence and routing details. Workflow roles and peer selection are
explained in [coga/workflows](../workflows/SKILL.md); the
[first-task walk](../first-task/SKILL.md) covers the prerequisites for a PR
with either one agent or a peer reviewer.

## Allowlists

`coga.toml` top level: `version`…500 tokens truncated…ing](../tickets/authoring/SKILL.md)) |
| `[telemetry]` | `enabled` (boolean only) | both; local overrides shared, including local true over shared false |

The split is deliberate. `[layout]` and `[autofix]` are team policy: one
clone must not resolve a context ref somewhere another clone does not.
`[upstream] checkouts` is the mirror image. It names absolute paths to other
repos on this machine, so it is accepted only locally and validated for
shape alone: a list of non-empty strings, `~` expanded, required to be
absolute. A path missing on disk still loads and is skipped by its consumer,
because failing config load would brick every command when a client repo
moves. `[authoring] agent` is local for the same reason: which agent an
operator authors tickets with (say, while one agent's quota is exhausted) is
a fact about that operator. Load checks only its shape; the name is checked
against `[agents]` when authoring resolves it, and `COGA_AUTHORING_AGENT`
overrides it. `user` is always local and never guessed
([coga/init](../init/SKILL.md)).

## Unknown keys fail loud

Any unrecognized key at any level of a fixed-schema table, in either file,
raises `ConfigError` naming the offender and listing the allowed keys. A
misspelled `[notification.slak]` therefore stops every config-loading command
instead of silently resolving to "no webhook".

Free-form maps are exempt because their keys are data: `[aliases]`,
`[extensions]` (a repo-owned namespace Coga passes through uninterpreted),
`[notification.slack.gifs]`, and `[notification.slack.users]`.

Known-but-removed or misplaced keys raise tailored errors **before** the
generic check, so the actionable message survives:

- `[assignees]` and `[megalaunch]` in `coga.toml`;
- `[secrets]` in `coga.local.toml` (secrets are declared inline on tickets);
- `[authoring]` in `coga.toml` (machine-local; the install-level default is
  `bootstrap/ticket`'s `agent:`);
- `[slack]` in either file (moved under `[notification.slack]`);
- `auto`, `skip_permissions`, `skip_permissions_argv` in any
  `[agents.<name>]`, reported against the file that contains them.

## `env:` indirection in config

Config values are otherwise literal. Exactly two fields run an `env:VAR`
reference through the shared resolver: `[notification.slack].webhook` and
`[notification.slack].important_webhook`. An unset
variable there resolves to "no webhook configured". An `env:VAR` written in
any other config field is a literal string, not an indirection, and `op://`
is not understood anywhere in config. Ticket `secrets:` are a separate,
fail-loud path.

## Other configuration surfaces

`owner` (the recurring operator), `[launch]` limits, and `[autofix]` are
owned by [coga/recurring](../recurring/SKILL.md). `[aliases]` expand to
Coga argv ([coga/cli](../cli/SKILL.md)).

Telemetry defaults on. Both `[telemetry]` layers are
validated even when overridden. No endpoint, key, cadence, or test bypass is
configurable. Delivery, state and payload belong to
[phone-home ticket](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/recurring/phone-home/ticket.md); git and notification switches remain
independent.

`[recurring].idle_days` is team policy and cannot be overridden locally.
Booleans, negative values and non-integers raise `ConfigError`. The activity
signal, calendar boundary and sweep overrides are owned by
[recurring scheduling](../recurring/scheduling/inactivity/SKILL.md).

`[log].retention_days` cannot be overridden locally. Booleans, negative values,
non-integers, non-table values and unknown keys fail config loading. Very large
positive integers saturate at `datetime.min` when computing the cutoff. Days
are local calendar days, matching timezone-free log envelopes: complete
unprotected events strictly before local midnight on today minus the window
expire. The boundary and future timestamps stay. The
[trim-log ticket](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/recurring/trim-log/ticket.md)
owns exceptions and its weekly schedule; its
[operations guide](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/recurring/trim-log/operations.md)
owns default-on adoption for existing repos.

# Writing to a ticket blackboard

The blackboard is everything below the `<!-- coga:blackboard -->` fence in a
ticket: working memory shared by human and agent and carried between
stateless sessions. Its live state is composed into every launch
([coga/prompt-composition](../prompt-composition/SKILL.md)); `coga/log.md`,

in the log.

## The fence

The fence counts only as a whole line: no leading indentation, optional
trailing whitespace. Markdown is not parsed, so an own-line fence inside a
code block counts, while an inline mention does not.

  unanchored `grep`/`sed`): a quoted fence in prose truncates the body.

  tickets legitimately have none.
- **Scope each edit.** Compute every transform on the blackboard region, never
  on whole-file text, so a `## Heading` pattern cannot hit the body, and never
  reformat the YAML while writing below the fence.

[coga/tickets](../tickets/SKILL.md) (agents: `contexts` and body sections).

with no live recorded checkout is left to Dream's retro pass, and one with a
live checkout is retirement debt that `coga retire <slug>` disposes of and
deletes ([Dream template](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/recurring/dream/ticket.md) owns that split). A section a writer rewrites
every run (a recurring template's state, Dream's own per-run report) is not
trimmed by hand either: the next run overwrites the edit, and
[coga/period-task](../period-task/SKILL.md) says to touch only your own keys.
Route it to its owner as a decision (attachment, exemption, or accepted
warning).

## Publishing cleanup

Draft synthesis and live-ticket size cleanup publish as Coga state through
[state publication](../state-publication/SKILL.md). The owner can edit directly
on control or track the cleanup in a workflow without branch or PR gates.
Ticket bodies, blackboards, and sibling attachments stay out of code PRs.

## What later passes do to content

- A replaced live value leaves the section; git keeps it.
- A replaced design moves into the single `## Superseded designs` section;
  the body keeps at most a one-line pointer. Keep rationale still needed for
  current work in live notes.
- A resolved blocker keeps its ask.
- A period task's blackboard is deleted at Dream's retro cleanup: durable
  gotchas go under `## Gotchas` for extraction and last-run state goes on the
  parent template's blackboard ([coga/period-task](../period-task/SKILL.md)).

## Concurrent writers

There is no ownership mutex; divergent workers are visible and recoverable in
git ([coga/launch](../launch/SKILL.md)). A `ticket.py` or other program that
writes a blackboard uses `blackboard.update_blackboard_under_barrier`, which
refuses rather than overwrite an intervening edit. Read the region
immediately before writing, prefer section appends to whole-region rewrites,
and keep writes as small as the change. Parser and race details are in
[blackboard IO](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/docs/contexts/coga-dev/internals/blackboard-io/SKILL.md);
cross-checkout reconciliation is in [coga/sync](../sync/SKILL.md).
"}

name: coga/tickets
description: The ticket file contract — frontmatter validation rules, who may write which part, the body regions that compose, and `owner:` reassignment and ticket relationships; task discovery and refs, and creating and authoring tickets, live in its leaves.
---

# Tickets

A ticket is one unit of work, git-backed while it lives and disposable once
done (what it taught moves into contexts): YAML frontmatter, a body, the fence
line `<!-- coga:blackboard -->`, then the blackboard region. The blackboard
writer's contract is [coga/blackboard](../blackboard/SKILL.md); status and
step movement are [coga/lifecycle](../lifecycle/SKILL.md).

New tickets carry a field guide as an HTML comment under `## Context`,
rendered from the `ticket.md` resource. It owns frontmatter and blackboard
field shapes; the rules below and in the base prompt hold whether or not a
ticket carries it.

## Leaves

- [coga/tickets/discovery](discovery/SKILL.md) — where tasks live, file
  versus directory form, parked and group directories, task refs, and
  finding a retired task in Git.
- [coga/tickets/authoring](authoring/SKILL.md) — `coga create`, the guided
  `coga ticket` interview and its authoring agent, and `coga show`.

## Frontmatter validation

- An activated task must have an `agent` naming a configured agent. Null,
  blank, unknown, or since-removed names fail validation. Activation fills
  an absent draft value with the configured default agent; default resolution
  is explained beside `default_agent` in the shipped `coga.toml`
  ([coga/configuration](../configuration/SKILL.md)).
- `contexts`, `skills`, `secrets`: absence is empty and an empty list is not
  written. A malformed falsy value (`contexts:` null, `""`, `0`) stays on disk
  so validation names it.
- Removed keys are errors (validate kind `removed-ticket-field`). Every writer
  refuses such a ticket; there is no compatibility reader. Recurring templates
  reject them at load.
- Extension fields are strings only, with no nesting and no canonical-name
  collisions. `coga validate` fails on a missing declared field or enum
  violation and only warns on an undeclared orphan key. Extensions reach
  prompts only as part of the ticket, not as a separate layer.

**Who writes what.** Agents may edit `contexts` and the body sections, plus
the blackboard; every other frontmatter field belongs to CLI commands and
humans (base prompt). A specialized authoring skill may grant an explicit
exception. `coga/log.md` is written only by CLI commands.

## Body regions

Only `## Description`, `## Context`, and the live blackboard reach the agent
([coga/prompt-composition](../prompt-composition/SKILL.md)). Each section runs
to the next `##` line, so any other `##` above the fence is **uncomposed**: a
`## Acceptance Criteria` or `## Proposed Shape`, and equally a `## What broke`
written after Description prose, which also cuts that Description short.
Text before the first real `##` heading is also uncomposed, including the
entire body when it has no such heading. A `##` inside a code fence is text.

Relocate rather than add headings. Spec material (acceptance criteria,
proposed shape, out of scope, evidence) goes as `###` subsections under
`## Description`, background under `## Context`, and working notes below the
fence. Coga does not compose extra `##` sections.

The drop is not silent. `coga validate` warns `uncomposed-section` on every
non-terminal ticket, naming each omitted heading or preamble and the repair;
`coga launch` and `--prompt-report` print the same diagnostic. A nonempty
Description does not suppress the preamble warning. While a body has omitted
material, validate reports it instead of `empty-description`, because the
write-up is already on disk. Terminal tickets are exempt.

## Owner and relationships

`owner:` is the human of record: owner steps route to that person, megalaunch
filters by owner, and notifications mention them. Reassign with
`coga owner <slug> <name>`; it preserves status, step, and body, rejects blank
or unchanged names and terminal records, and writes an audit line without a
Slack post.

- An `in_progress` agent step must stop and be paused first.
- An `in_progress` **owner-held gate** instead requires `--assist-stopped`:
  the human attests, from outside that ticket's supervised session, that any
  assisting agent has stopped. The gate is preserved so its new owner can
  bump it. Coga has no live-session registry to check this.
- A supervised session cannot reassign its own ticket, and an outstanding
  `launch_generation` is refused. A plain or `released:` claim recovers
  through `coga launch <slug>`; finish or pause that session, then retry. A
  `pending:` claim needs the human to reconcile local and control evidence.
  Never clear a claim merely to force reassignment.
- A publication failure exits 75; refresh and reconcile control before
  retrying.

Ticket-to-ticket relationships use the dependency and supersession
conventions in [coga/lifecycle](../lifecycle/SKILL.md), not
`dependencies:` or `superseded_by:` frontmatter. Successor-side "this blocks
X" prose is a human pointer, not machine-readable ordering.

description: The ticket file contract — frontmatter validation rules, who may write which part, the body regions that compose, and `owner:` reassignment and ticket relationships; task discovery and refs, and creating and authoring tickets, live in its leaves.
---

# Tickets

A ticket is one unit of work, git-backed while it lives and disposable once
done (what it taught moves into contexts): YAML frontmatter, a body, the fence
line `<!-- coga:blackboard -->`, then the blackboard region. The blackboard
writer's contract is [coga/blackboard](../blackboard/SKILL.md); status and
step movement are [coga/lifecycle](../lifecycle/SKILL.md).

New tickets carry a field guide as an HTML comment under `## Context`,
rendered from the `ticket.md` resource. It owns frontmatter and blackboard
field shapes; the rules below and in the base prompt hold whether or not a
ticket carries it.

## Leaves

- [coga/tickets/discovery](discovery/SKILL.md) — where tasks live, file
  versus directory form, parked and group directories, task refs, and
  finding a retired task in Git.
- [coga/tickets/authoring](authoring/SKILL.md) — `coga create`, the guided
  `coga ticket` interview and its authoring agent, and `coga show`.

## Frontmatter validation

- An activated task must have an `agent` naming a configured agent. Null,
  blank, unknown, or since-removed names fail validation. Activation fills
  an absent draft value with the configured default agent; default resolution
  is explained beside `default_agent` in the shipped `coga.toml`
  ([coga/configuration](../configuration/SKILL.md)).
- `contexts`, `skills`, `secrets`: absence is empty and an empty list is not
  written. A malformed falsy value (`contexts:` null, `""`, `0`) stays on disk
  so validation names it.
- Removed keys are errors (validate kind `removed-ticket-field`). Every writer
  refuses such a ticket; there is no compatibility reader. Recurring templates
  reject them at load.
- Extension fields are strings only, with no nesting and no canonical-name
  collisions. `coga validate` fails on a missing declared field or enum
  violation and only warns on an undeclared orphan key. Extensions reach
  prompts only as part of the ticket, not as a separate layer.

**Who writes what.** Agents may edit `contexts` and the body sections, plus
the blackboard; every other frontmatter field belongs to CLI commands and
humans (base prompt). A specialized authoring skill may grant an explicit
exception. `coga/log.md` is written only by CLI commands.

## Body regions

Only `## Description`, `## Context`, and the live blackboard reach the agent
([coga/prompt-composition](../prompt-composition/SKILL.md)). Each section runs
to the next `##` line, so any other `##` above the fence is **uncomposed**: a
`## Acceptance Criteria` or `## Proposed Shape`, and equally a `## What broke`
written after Description prose, which also cuts that Description short.
Text before the first real `##` heading is also uncomposed, including the
entire body when it has no such heading. A `##` inside a code fence is text.

Relocate rather than add headings. Spec material (acceptance criteria,
proposed shape, out of scope, evidence) goes as `###` subsections under
`## Description`, background under `## Context`, and working notes below the
fence. Coga does not compose extra `##` sections.

The drop is not silent. `coga validate` warns `uncomposed-section` on every
non-terminal ticket, naming each omitted heading or preamble and the repair;
`coga launch` and `--prompt-report` print the same diagnostic. A nonempty
Description does not suppress the preamble warning. While a body has omitted
material, validate reports it instead of `empty-description`, because the
write-up is already on disk. Terminal tickets are exempt.

## Owner and relationships

`owner:` is the human of record: owner steps route to that person, megalaunch
filters by owner, and notifications mention them. Reassign with
`coga owner <slug> <name>`; it preserves status, step, and body, rejects blank
or unchanged names and terminal records, and writes an audit line without a
Slack post.

- An `in_progress` agent step must stop and be paused first.
- An `in_progress` **owner-held gate** instead requires `--assist-stopped`:
  the human attests, from outside that ticket's supervised session, that any
  assisting agent has stopped. The gate is preserved so its new owner can
  bump it. Coga has no live-session registry to check this.
- A supervised session cannot reassign its own ticket, and an outstanding
  `launch_generation` is refused. A plain or `released:` claim recovers
  through `coga launch <slug>`; finish or pause that session, then retry. A
  `pending:` claim needs the human to reconcile local and control evidence.
  Never clear a claim merely to force reassignment.
- A publication failure exits 75; refresh and reconcile control before
  retrying.

Ticket-to-ticket relationships use the dependency and supersession
conventions in [coga/lifecycle](../lifecycle/SKILL.md), not
`dependencies:` or `superseded_by:` frontmatter. Successor-side "this blocks
X" prose is a human pointer, not machine-readable ordering.

def last_updated_map(cfg: Config, refs: list[TaskRef]) -> dict[str, datetime]:
    """Each task's last-activity timestamp — the `Updated` column's source.

    The primary source is the repo-global log (one pass builds every task's
    last-activity stamp). The log only knows a task by its ref, so it goes
    silent when a task directory is moved (append-only lines keep the old ref)
    or when a ticket reached disk without passing through a logging command;
    git saw both, so one `git log` pass backstops the blanks — see
    `last_commit_times`. Tasks with no stamp from either source are absent.

    Shared by `coga status` and the megalaunch picker so both views read one
    clock.
    """
    activity = last_activity_map(cfg)
    # Only tasks the log is silent on need git's history, and usually there
    # are none or a handful — walking every commit under `tasks/` for them
    # dominated `coga status` on a long-lived repo.
    uncovered = [
        f"{ref.id_slug}.md" if ref.file_form else ref.id_slug
        for ref in refs
        if ref.id_slug not in activity
    ]
    git_updated = _git_updated_by_slug(refs, last_commit_times(cfg, uncovered))
    out: dict[str, datetime] = {}
    for ref in refs:
        stamp = activity.get(ref.id_slug) or git_updated.get(ref.id_slug)
        if stamp is not None:
            out[ref.id_slug] = stamp
    return out
